question.worked_solution:
We can find the roots of a quadratic equation using the quadratic formula:

$$
x=\frac{-b\pm \sqrt{{b}^{2}-4ac}}{2a}
$$

In this case, the coefficients are $a=-2,b=4,$ and $c=-8.$ Substituting these values into the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{(4)^{2}-4(-2)(-8)}}{2(-2)} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{16-64}}{-4} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{-48}}{-4} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm 4\sqrt{-3}}{-4} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm 4\sqrt{3}\,\text{i}}{-4} \\  & =1\pm \sqrt{3}\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation has two solutions, $x=1+\sqrt{3}\,\text{i}$ and $x=1-\sqrt{3}\,\text{i}.$
